text:
zoe: Quick sync — we need to lock the scope for the auth work in the next sprint. Customers want project-scoped API keys + rotation hooks.

matt: Agreed. Narrow question: do we support both project and org keys from day 1 or ship project-only and add org later?

eli: Project-first seems lowest friction. Org keys add a lot of UX + billing/quotas work.

zoe: +1 project-first. But we must design the schema so org can be added without breaking migrations.

sanjay: Important: rotation impact on long-lived KV caches and streaming sessions. If key changes, do we force session kill? customers will ask.

matt: Implementation note: session tokens reference key_id. If rotated we can keep old key valid for X minutes to drain KV caches. Suggest configurable grace window.

carla: Console needs a "Create project key" flow and "Rotate" button with clear warnings. Also audit log entry for rotate + who triggered.

zoe: Launch criteria proposal: (1) project-scoped keys create/read/delete in Console + API, (2) rotation endpoint + SDK helper, (3) audit events emitted, (4) docs + migration guide. Thoughts?

eli: Add: server-side validation of key -> project mapping to prevent cross-project calls. And per-key rate-limits scoped to the project.

matt: For rate-limits we can reuse per-project bucket. Need to decide if a key inherits project quotas or has its own quotas. Recommend keys inherit project quotas; simpler.

sanjay: Operational risk: rotating keys can increase request spikiness when clients retry. Recommend rollout docs suggest staggered rotation and SDK auto-retry with backoff.

zoe: Customer asks for rotation webhook so they can trigger CI/CD secrets update. Can we support a "rotation.completed" webhook?

matt: Yes — small event with key_id old/new and project_id. Security: webhook payload should sign with HMAC; store webhook secret per project.

carla: UX: show key age, last rotated, and disable option. Also surface if key is used by Dedicated/Private vs Hosted. Some customers need separation.

eli: One more: function/tool-calling implications. If a key is project-scoped, tools owned by org might need broader access. We need a mapping: tool-level permissions vs API key scope.

zoe: Action items: 
- matt: design API endpoints (create, list, rotate, disable) + rotation grace window default = 300s.
- eli: auth model doc: key -> project/org mapping, inheritance rules, rate-limit behavior.
- carla: wireframe console flows + audit UX.
- sanjay: run a short runbook draft for rotation incidents.

matt: Sketch for API: 
```
POST /v1/keys
{ "project_id": "proj_123", "name": "embed-service", "scopes": ["completions","embeddings"] }
POST /v1/keys/:key_id/rotate
{ "grace_seconds": 300 }
```

sanjay: Note: rotation endpoint should return both new_key.value (one-time) and key_id for lookup. We'll need help desks to flag leaked old keys.

zoe: Prioritization: ship project keys + rotation + audit in sprint 1. Org keys + console billing mapping in sprint 2. Docs and SDK helpers included in sprint 1 for basic rotation.

carla: Risk flags for PM doc: migration complexity for customers with embedded long-lived keys, on-prem customers with air-gapped rotation, and Dedicated customers that manage keys via KMS.

eli: For Dedicated/Private: support BYOK and rotation hooks that call their KMS. Add compatibility tests.

zoe: OK — I'll update roadmap entry and acceptance criteria. If nobody objects, I'll post RFC with the API contract and wireframes tomorrow.

matt: no objections. :thumbsup:

carla: :+1:

ops-bot: Reminder — create incident postmortem template for any major key rotation outage.

zoe: Thanks team — assigning tickets now.
